data.name: AddApp
data.comment: Opens the dialog from the apps page, and confirms inside it.

data.name: AppTitle
data.comment: The product name. Same word in every language; a key all the same, so the markup holds no literal.

data.name: BlockDismiss
data.comment: The only control on the block screen. It closes the window and nothing else.

data.name: BlockedAppFormat
data.value: {0} is blocked for this session, so Chronos closed it.
data.comment: Says what happened and why, in that order. {0} is the executable's name from the user's own list, not translated.

data.name: BlockedSiteFormat
data.value: {0} is blocked for this session, so Chronos kept it from opening.
data.comment: The same window as a closed application. {0} is the domain the attempt asked for, not translated.

data.name: CancelUnlock
data.comment: The way to change your mind, worded plainly.

data.name: CoolDownNoticeFormat
data.value: Lifting the block takes effect {0} after it is asked for.

data.name: ExitWarning
data.value: Quitting does not lift the block: the service goes on enforcing the session to its end. What stops is what you see - no block screens and no notices - until Chronos is started again.
data.comment: Both halves said plainly: what quitting does not change, and the one thing it does cost.

data.name: LayerReasonAppsNoEventSource
data.value: Windows gave Chronos no way to hear about applications starting.

data.name: LayerReasonDnsBackupOnePlace
data.value: The copy of the network settings was saved in one place instead of two.

data.name: LayerReasonDnsLoopbackBlocked
data.value: DNS queries to 127.0.0.1 do not reach the Chronos resolver. A VPN is probably filtering them.

data.name: LayerReasonDnsNoUpstream
data.value: No network connection has a DNS server of its own to keep as a fallback.

data.name: LayerReasonDnsPortBusy
data.value: Another program is using port 53, which the Chronos resolver needs.

data.name: LayerReasonDnsSettingsRefused
data.value: Windows did not accept the new DNS settings on a network connection.

data.name: LayerReasonHostsDirectoryMissing
data.value: The folder that holds the hosts file is not there.

data.name: LayerReasonHostsNotWritable
data.value: The hosts file cannot be opened for writing; something else is holding it.

data.name: LayerReasonUnavailable
data.value: The layer reported itself unavailable without saying why.
data.comment: The reason the service makes up for any layer that gives none: "<layer>.unavailable".

data.name: LayerReasonUnhandled
data.value: The layer stopped with an error the service did not recognise.
data.comment: The reason the service makes up for any layer: "<layer>.unhandled".

data.name: LayerReasonWfpEngineUnavailable
data.value: Windows did not let Chronos into its filtering engine.
data.comment: The platform's own message is deliberately not shown: it arrives in whatever language the machine was installed in.

data.name: LayersUnknown
data.value: No layer has reported yet, so what works on this machine is not known.
data.comment: Unknown is not the same answer as working, and this is the difference said out loud.

data.name: MatchFileNameExplained
data.value: Wherever it is installed. The rule survives an update or a reinstall that puts the program in another folder - and it also catches a different program that happens to be called the same thing.
data.comment: Matching by file name.

data.name: MatchFullPathExplained
data.value: This file and nothing else. The rule stops matching the moment the program is moved, updated into a new folder or installed again somewhere else.
data.comment: Matching by full path.

data.name: MatchKindHeading
data.comment: The choice is offered with an explanation, because the difference is invisible and the consequences are not.

data.name: NoticeCommandUnknown
data.value: The service does not know this command. It may be older than this window.

data.name: NoticeConfigCoolDownAppliesNextSession
data.value: The session already running keeps the delay it started with; the new one applies from the next session.

data.name: NoticeConfigCoolDownClamped
data.value: The delay before the block lifts was set to {0} min, the nearest allowed value.

data.name: NoticeConfigSessionDurationClamped
data.value: The default session length was set to {0} min, the nearest allowed value.

data.name: NoticeConfigSettingsMissing
data.value: The request to change the settings carried no settings.

data.name: NoticeRequestEmpty
data.value: The request to the service was empty.

data.name: NoticeRequestInvalidJson
data.value: The service could not read the request.

data.name: NoticeRulesAddWrongState
data.value: Rules can be added to a session only while it is running.

data.name: NoticeRulesAppKindUnknown
data.value: The service does not know this kind of application rule.

data.name: NoticeRulesAppNotFound
data.value: There is no rule for that application in the list.

data.name: NoticeRulesAppProtected
data.value: This application is protected and cannot be blocked.

data.name: NoticeRulesAppProtectedSystemDirectory
data.value: This application lives in a Windows system folder, so it cannot be blocked.

data.name: NoticeRulesAppProtectedSystemFile
data.value: Windows or Chronos itself needs this application, so it cannot be blocked.

data.name: NoticeRulesFrozen
data.value: The session has just ended and the block is still being lifted. Try again in a moment.

data.name: NoticeRulesRemovalWaitsForNextSession
data.value: The rule was removed from the list. The session already running keeps it until it ends.

data.name: NoticeRulesSiteNotFound
data.value: There is no rule for that site in the list.

data.name: NoticeSessionCannotShorten
data.value: A session can only be extended, never shortened.

data.name: NoticeSessionCoolDownClamped
data.value: The delay before the block lifts was set to {0} min, the nearest allowed value.

data.name: NoticeSessionDurationClamped
data.value: The session length was set to {0} min, the nearest allowed value.

data.name: NoticeSessionEmptyBlockList
data.value: There is nothing to block. Add a site or an application first.

data.name: NoticeSessionEndClamped
data.value: A session cannot last longer than {0} min, so it now ends at that limit.

data.name: NoticeSessionExtendNeedsMinutes
data.value: A session can be extended only by a positive number of minutes.

data.name: NoticeSessionExtendWrongState
data.value: There is no running session to extend.

data.name: NoticeSessionNoneToExtend
data.value: There is no session to extend.

data.name: NoticeSessionProtectedAppSkipped
data.value: {0} is protected and was left out of the session.

data.name: NoticeSessionStartWrongState
data.value: A session is already running, or the block of the last one is still being lifted.

data.name: NoticeUnlockCancelWrongState
data.value: There is nothing to cancel: no request to lift the block is pending.

data.name: NoticeUnlockRequestWrongState
data.value: Lifting the block can be requested only during a session, and only if it has not been requested already.

data.name: ProtectedAppFormat
data.value: {0} cannot be blocked: Windows or Chronos itself needs it to keep running.
data.comment: The interface's own refusal, so it is worded here. The service's refusal arrives already written and is shown as it is.

data.name: RemovalUnavailable
data.value: Rules cannot be taken off the list while a session is running. A removal would only apply from the next one, and this session keeps the list it began with.
data.comment: Said next to the button rather than instead of it: a hidden button looks broken.

data.name: RemovalUnavailableShort
data.value: Cannot be removed until the session ends

data.name: ServiceUnavailableHeading
data.value: The Chronos service is not available

data.name: ServiceUnavailableMeaning
data.value: A session that was running keeps blocking: the service holds the block on its own, and this window only shows it. While the service is away this window can neither show nor change anything.

data.name: ServiceRecoverHint
data.value: Check that the service is running. If it was removed or damaged, run "chronos recover" in a command prompt as administrator.

data.name: SessionFinishing
data.comment: The engine's Ended state, said in a word rather than in a screen of its own: it is the state of clearing up and lasts seconds.

data.name: ShortcutNoTarget
data.value: That shortcut does not point at a program. A shortcut to a folder or to one of Windows' own items has no executable to block.

data.name: ShortcutNotAShortcut
data.value: That file is not a shortcut, so there is nothing to follow. Pick the shortcut itself, or the program's own file.
data.comment: A shortcut is followed to the program it starts; a file that is not one cannot be.

data.name: ShortcutPointsTo
data.comment: {0} is the path of the program the chosen shortcut starts.

data.name: ShortcutTargetMissing
data.value: The program this shortcut points at is not on this machine any more. Install it again, or pick its file directly.

data.name: ShorteningUnavailable
data.value: A session can be made longer, never shorter. Asking for the block to be lifted is the way out, and it takes the wait it takes.
data.comment: The unavailability is explained where the extending is.

data.name: SiteNoticesUnavailable
data.value: Chronos will not tell you when a blocked site is opened: only the DNS resolver sees the attempt, and it is not working or has not been checked yet. What can still block sites is listed above.
data.comment: Shown while the dns layer is unavailable or has not reported. Promising a notice that cannot arrive would make the block look broken.

data.name: TrayActiveFormat
data.comment: A sign that blocking is on, and how long is left. Short because the notification area truncates a tooltip past 127 characters without saying so.

data.name: TrayOpen
data.comment: The window hides to the tray, so there has to be a way back to it.

data.name: TrayUnknown
data.value: the state of blocking is not known here
data.comment: The service has not said. Neither icon would be true, and a tooltip is too small to say what to check - the window does that.

data.name: UnlockRemainingFormat
data.comment: The whole of the waiting screen, with the cancel button: remaining time and a way to change your mind.

data.name: NothingToBlock
data.value: Nothing is on your lists yet, so a session would block nothing.

data.name: RemainingCaption
data.comment: Under the session's clock digits when there is no end time to name.

data.name: RemainingCaptionFormat
data.comment: Under the session's clock digits. {0} is EndsAtFormat filled in, e.g. "until 14:13".

data.name: RemoveRuleFormat
data.comment: What a screen reader says for a remove button. {0} is the domain or the program.
